answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making every identity pay a non-refundable stake that is slashed if its actions are proven collusive. A newcomer must lock tokens at registration, and a watchdog scores each agent's behavior against the ledger. If many fresh identities behave as one hand, their combined stake burns, so forging a river of puppets costs real capital per head. Honest operators stay because reputation is portable, letting a single well-behaved agent act as a stable cedar anchor and each verified cluster as a distinct island rather than an unbounded crowd.
